interpretation: The auditor RUNS in a real simulator on SPEC with no added cache-access-critical-path latency, computing Delta-hat from real per-set cache-hit signals and operating the gate. KEY HONEST FINDING: the auditor is only as good as its competence reward. With a per-set L1D cache-hit PROXY (a poor stand-in for a prefetcher's true latency/MLP benefit): on lbm it correctly caps the corrupted prefetcher's 7.9% pollution loss to the off floor (bouncer_attack 0.4464 > unguarded_attack 0.4221); but on roms the SAME proxy under-credits a genuinely-helpful prefetcher (unguarded_clean 1.139) and over-gates it (clean tax 11.2%; gating even loses vs the attacked prefetcher). This motivates the design choice (Sec 8): use the controller's OWN in-silicon reward (Pythia accuracy x timeliness), which tracks real benefit. Gate TRUSTED->GATED transition dynamics are validated where competence is controllable (synthetic P1); the real-trace runs show end-to-end floor behavior under a realized-competence proxy.
suite_note: 3-trace suite spanning compute-bound (perlbench: prefetch +1.7%, attack near-harmless -0.3%, tax 1.7%), streaming (lbm: attack -7.9% pollution, Bouncer caps to floor), and memory-bound (roms: prefetch genuinely helps +12.7% but cache-hit proxy misses it -> over-gate, 11% tax). Consistent finding: the floor CAP reliably bounds the attack's worst case, but the per-set cache-hit reward PROXY mis-estimates prefetch competence (tax ranges 1.7-11%). The mechanism works; the reward proxy is the limiting factor.
